The derivation begins with the fundamental decomposition of total variance into intra-cluster (b) and inter-cluster (c) components. By establishing the algebraic identity v = sqrt(b^3 / (b+c)), we isolate the intrinsic dispersion parameter b through rigorous substitution of empirical constants. This forms the primary sovereign primitive: the Variance Decomposition Kernel. However, estimating b via pairwise differences introduces a profound topological constraint. While a cluster of size n yields n(n-1)/2 pairwise differences, the vector space spanned by these differences is intrinsically degenerate. The sum of signed differences around any closed loop within the cluster must vanish, imposing linear dependencies. Consequently, the maximum rank of the difference matrix is strictly bounded by n-1. Ignoring this rank constraint—the Independent Difference Rank primitive—leads to an arbitrary oversampling of the underlying information manifold. In GSI, this translates to treating correlated kinship data as independent Bernoulli trials, severely underestimating posterior uncertainty. The failure mode is explicit: selecting three differences from a trio of brothers violates the n-1 bound, injecting artificial precision. Thus, the dual operators—one algebraic, one topological—must be applied simultaneously to extract unbiased parameters from clustered biological or tactical data.
